title: Add structured validation state and evidence rules to the task and audit process
description:
## Summary
The 2026-09-12 validation/process audit found that evidence discipline, not code quality, is now the binding constraint: source completion is repeatedly reported as behavioural completion, acceptance criteria mix deterministic facts with visual judgement, regressions are added without naming the mechanism they target, and audit findings vanish during synthesis when they are too small to deserve a ticket.

## User Mandate
> "As always, look for recurring issues and patterns of bugs or mistakes that we can add process safeguards against"

STRICT. This task exists to add process safeguards against recurring evidence failures. Do not relax, re-scope, or silently drop any safeguard listed in Scope.

## Scope
- VT-01/VT-08: add a standard validation-state vocabulary to the task contract: `implemented`, `unit-tested`, `unity-tested`, `user-accepted`, plus `blockers[]` and `lastValidatedCommit`.
- VT-03: require acceptance criteria to pair any visual judgement with a measurable invariant.
- VT-09: require every regression to name the historical failure mechanism, why the fixture triggers it, and the pre/post fix expectation.
- VT-02: require Unity evidence to name Unity version, fixture/scene, scenario or test count, commit SHA, and console cleanliness.
- VT-04/F-20: make a per-finding disposition ledger mandatory in every audit synthesis (source finding -> verification result -> mechanism -> owner -> disposition). No finding may disappear for lack of a ticket.
- VT-05: treat the audit report ID as a durable evidence key and cite it from task comments.
- VT-10: require performance claims to state a workload envelope.
- VT-12: require an audit-placement check that the report is committed on the branch it claims.
- Out of scope: reopening CI (TSK-0123, Rejected).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `.github/skills/task-tracker/SKILL.md` defines the validation vocabulary, the required `## Validation` block, and the regression-mechanism rule.
- `.github/skills/unity-validation/SKILL.md` defines the required Unity evidence identity fields.
- `.github/skills/cc-audit-synthesis/SKILL.md` requires the disposition ledger table and an audit-placement verification step as completion-checklist items.
- One existing task record is updated to demonstrate the vocabulary end to end.
- A re-run of a synthesis against this same audit batch produces zero findings with an empty disposition cell.

## Validation
- Skill files re-read after edit; each new rule present and unambiguous.
- Sample task record re-read to confirm the vocabulary applies without breaking the required body headings.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- No code or serialized-data change, so no Unity gate is required for this task.

## Findings
- Verified: `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` enforces `createdAtUtc`/`updatedAtUtc`/`revision` but has no validation-state or blocker fields, so the audit's requested structure is not yet expressible.
- Verified: the `task-tracker` skill currently requires a `## Validation` section but does not define its vocabulary.
- Verified: `cc-audit-synthesis` already requires "an explicit unresolved disposition" per material claim, but does not mandate the ledger table shape or an audit-placement check.
- Recurrence: the same "small findings are lost in synthesis" pattern was recorded on 2026-09-09 (meta-synthesis) and again on 2026-09-12 (deep-dive F-20).

## Blockers
- The MemorySmith task schema does not expose structured fields for validation state; the vocabulary must live in the stable markdown body convention until the schema supports it.

## Next Step
Edit the three skill files, then update one task record as the worked example.
